newsitem.title: USA: June Brent mostly lower in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: June Brent mostly lower in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: North Sea bellwether Brent traded mostly lower in heavy late U.S. paper dealings, traders said.
June Brent partial cargoes traded between $18.10 and $18.15 a barrel.
The June contract on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) settled at $18.14.
The May contract expired today, with the last trade down 23 cents a barrel at $17.96 on bearish expectations for the American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory data, traders said.
The data revealed that U.S. crude stocks were up 2.97 million barrels, while gasoline was up 3.63 million barrels in the week ending April 11.
Distillate stocks were up 2.59 million barrels.
Also in the U.S. aftermarket, May/June Brent traded at minus 30 cents.
Immediately preceding the close, the intermonth spread changed hands at minus 29 cents.
A June/July spread traded at minus 15 cents, also right before the close, traders said.
